title: AI Follow-Up for Unpaid Medical Claims and AR Recovery
summary: See how AI can follow up on unpaid medical claims, cut payer hold work, support appeals, and test recovery on a real hospital backlog before rollout.
body_markdown:
*By[Vanessa C](https://www.linkedin.com/in/vanessa-couch-laguana-ehrc-crcr-b591239b/) , Head of RCM, LunaBill*


**Summary:** Yes, AI can follow up on unpaid medical claims by handling rules-based, evidence-driven tasks such as claim status checks, eligibility verification, remittance confirmation, payer calls, and resubmissions. It automates repeatable tasks, allowing human specialists to focus on complex appeals and patient-facing decisions, thereby improving AR recovery by moving claims from waiting lists to active queues.


A claims specialist logs in at 7:30 AM and finds 400 unpaid accounts older than 60 days, three payer portals asking for password resets, and hold times that average 45 minutes per call. The American Hospital Association reported in 2025 that[hospitals spent $43 billion](https://www.aha.org/costsofcaring) trying to collect payments insurers owe for care already delivered. Most of the drag shows up in aging AR, where people repeat status checks, hunt for missing remits, and resend rejected submissions.


Revenue cycle leaders staring at that pileup keep asking whether AI can chase unpaid medical claims without creating compliance trouble or breaking billing work. They have a point.


Machine learning systems can handle rules-based, evidence-driven AR follow-up across payer portals, automated phone calls, remittance matching, and resubmissions. The gain comes from stripping out repetitive admin work so hospital staff can spend time on hard denials and patient financial counseling. Cash collection improves when aging inventory moves out of dormant worklists and into active operating cycles. The real test is whether software can sit inside the billing stack, leave behind verifiable audit trails, and write valid encounter notes back to the patient accounting system.


## Can AI follow up on unpaid medical claims?


Turning denial codes into text blurbs does not close an account. An unpaid balance still needs verified claim status, proof of timely filing, payer-specific fixes, or an appeal packet, and medical billing follow-up works only when the system follows the claim from first look to payment posting.


Automating claim status checks cuts manual hold time only if the software handles the whole payer exchange. That means logging into payer portals, moving through IVR phone trees, waiting on hold, talking with payer representatives, and recording reference numbers. Scripted scrapers break down when a portal marks an account pending, flags a missing coordination of benefits form, or says no claim is on file.


Unassisted artificial intelligence still struggles in messy hospital settings.


A 2026 HealthAdminBench evaluation found that the leading computer-use model[completed 36.3% of tasks](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.09937) across simulated electronic health records and payer portals. Patient financial services teams should read that as a hard boundary. Generic desktop models fail without healthcare-specific workflows, strict validation rules, and built-in human escalation paths.


Clinical disputes and sensitive patient conversations have to stay with human staff. Appeals involving medical necessity, outside clinical review, and conversations with patients call for experienced judgment that billing departments should not hand to automated queues. Supervised automation works best when software clears the high-volume transactional backlog, leaving credentialed billing specialists free to work high-dollar contested denials.


## What work should AI take from the AR queue?


Routine administrative tasks with clear procedural paths make the safest starting point for AR automation. High-value assignments include checking active coverage, confirming 835 remittance data, fixing mismatched payer IDs, updating coordination of benefits details, and retransmitting scrubbed claims through clearinghouses. Hospital billing managers can watch these high-volume actions every day because each one produces a clear, verifiable result.


LunaBill deploys a coordinated team of 13 specialized AI agents that works the AR queue from start to finish. The system runs[AI-driven payer portal status checks](https://lunabill.com/) across portals like[Availity](https://lunabill.com/availity/) and Waystar, dials payers directly to move through IVR trees, waits for live representatives, pulls out denial details, and generates appeal packages. For accounts that need technical updates, LunaBill corrects payer IDs or coordination of benefits errors, resubmits claims through the hospital's clearinghouse, and writes reference numbers and call records back to[Epic](https://lunabill.com/epic/) ,[Cerner](https://lunabill.com/cerner/) , or GoRev without forcing billers into a separate application.


Automated appeal production cuts labor hours for business office teams when software matches root CARC and RARC codes (the claim adjustment reason codes and remittance advice remark codes payers return) with the right medical documentation and correct payer mailing addresses. Programmatic appeal generation removes the administrative delay that lets claims run past contractual timely filing limits.


Payment posting still has to happen after automated follow-up. Unposted transactions distort financial reporting, and an account stays unresolved until the payer reference number, check details, and line-item payment data write back to the core patient accounting system, keeping the business office from working settled balances.


## What changed in payer calls, appeals and attachments?


Payer phone operations shifted rapidly once revenue cycle platforms separated automated call management from clinical decision-making. In October 2026, Knack RCM[announced plans to use voice agents](https://knackrcm.com/resources/press-releases/knack-rcm-partners-with-prosper-ai/) to handle routine telephone calls and claim follow-up so staff could dedicate their attention to complex appeals.


Appeal workflows follow that same division of labor, using software to construct the documentation package while revenue cycle specialists approve the submission. In September 2026, Oracle Health[announced AI appeal management](https://www.oracle.com/news/announcement/oracle-health-advances-revenue-cycle-management-with-ai-2026-09-23/) capabilities designed to detect reimbursement variances and assemble formal appeal documents. Around the same time, Knowtion Health[launched an AI-assisted appeals partnership](https://www.knowtionhealth.com/learning-center/press-release-knowtion-and-ghamut-launch-strategic-partnership) with Ghamut to accelerate complex denial reviews.


Federal regulators are simultaneously converting documentation exchange from a manual fax process into an auditable digital standard. The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services issued a final rule in May 2026 establishing[electronic claims-attachment standards](https://www.cms.gov/newsroom/fact-sheets/administrative-simplification-adoption-standards-health-care-claims-attachments-transactions) , requiring healthcare providers and health plans to adopt standard transactions within 24 months. Standardized electronic attachments mean automated follow-up tools must maintain detailed documentation trails showing exactly when medical records arrived at the payer.


Initial denials by health plans frequently unravel when hospitals challenge them with supporting documentation. An HHS Office of Inspector General study in 2022 revealed that[18% of sampled denied payment requests](https://oig.hhs.gov/reports/all/2022/some-medicare-advantage-organization-denials-of-prior-authorization-requests-raise-concerns-about-beneficiary-access-to-medically-necessary-care/) by Medicare Advantage organizations actually satisfied Medicare coverage rules and billing terms. Leaving those improper denials untouched in aging AR surrenders earned cash that an organized appeal protocol can help recover.


## How should a revenue cycle leader test AI without platform risk?


A controlled evaluation begins on historical aged receivables rather than on simulated accounts. Patient financial services directors should assign a defined block of unpaid balances, establish explicit boundaries for automated actions, specify permissions for EHR write-back, and mandate an audit trail that timestamps every portal query, call recording, denial classification, and clearinghouse resubmission.


Revenue cycle leaders evaluating an automation partner should review five baseline operational criteria:


1. Compatibility with your existing clearinghouses, payer portals, and billing software without forcing your staff to adopt another software interface.
2. Explicit routing rules that separate automated transactional tasks from exceptions requiring human intervention.
3. Verifiable evidence capture for every payer call, including rep names, call reference numbers, and complete disposition notes.
4. Defined review steps for denial classification, appeal letter generation, and claims resubmission before files leave your organization.
5. Concrete targets for cash recovered, average touch time per account, and reduction in aged balances over 60 days to determine pilot success.


Mapping the path of an unadjudicated claim from initial submission through status verification, dispute resolution, and payment posting reveals where manual touches choke cash flow. Revenue cycle teams should examine end-to-end claim follow-up across their current systems to establish realistic baseline metrics before initiating vendor pilots.


## How to start AI follow-up on aged AR


Assign a single aging AR bucket where collection procedures follow predictable paths and staff spend excessive hours on hold. Direct automated tools toward repetitive payer interactions: portal queries, telephone follow-up, appeal packet preparation, clearinghouse resubmissions, and balance updates where write-back is enabled.


Run a targeted pilot on genuine aged accounts, require payer-specific resolution metrics, and set strict protocols that escalate complex clinical disputes to human billers. Revenue cycle executives should verify system audit trails and call logs before inspecting summary analytics, confirming that transactions reached payers directly.


Unpaid claims yield cash once accounts receive prompt payer inquiries, timely correction of billing errors, supported appeals, or posted remittances. The immediate step is scoping a pilot on a bounded slice of aged AR with defined recovery targets, working inside existing systems without added software disruption.


## Frequently Asked Questions


### Can AI handle follow-up on unpaid medical claims?


Yes, AI can manage follow-up on unpaid medical claims by automating tasks like claim status checks, eligibility verification, remittance confirmation, and payer calls. This allows human specialists to focus on complex appeals and patient-facing decisions, improving AR recovery by moving claims from waiting lists to active queues.


### What tasks can AI automate in the AR process?


AI can automate routine administrative tasks such as checking active coverage, confirming remittance data, fixing mismatched payer IDs, updating coordination of benefits details, and retransmitting scrubbed claims through clearinghouses. These tasks produce clear, verifiable results, making them ideal for automation.


### How does AI improve the efficiency of payer calls and appeals?


AI improves efficiency by separating automated call management from clinical decision-making, allowing staff to focus on complex appeals. AI constructs documentation packages for appeals while specialists approve submissions. This division of labor accelerates the process and ensures that claims are handled efficiently.


### What should revenue cycle leaders consider when testing AI for AR recovery?


Revenue cycle leaders should start with historical aged receivables, establish boundaries for automated actions, specify EHR write-back permissions, and ensure an audit trail for every action. They should also evaluate compatibility with existing systems, evidence capture, and set concrete targets for cash recovery and reduction in aged balances.


### What role does LunaBill play in AI-driven AR recovery?


LunaBill deploys a team of specialized AI agents to manage the AR queue from start to finish. It performs AI-driven payer portal status checks, dials payers, retrieves denial details, and generates appeal packages. LunaBill also corrects errors, resubmits claims, and writes back data to systems like Epic, Cerner, or GoRev, streamlining the AR process.


### Which unpaid claims should stay with human staff?


Appeals involving medical necessity, outside clinical review, clinical disputes, and conversations with patients should stay with experienced human staff. AI works best on the high-volume transactional backlog, leaving credentialed billing specialists free to work high-dollar contested denials.
